# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (first iteration of run)
- Strategy tried: multi-lever candidate in one pass — code guards (payment normalize + single-method amount auto-fill) as the primary lever, enriched returns on 3 write tools for the communicate-amount cluster, and additive prompt rules for the no-write stall. Bias toward CODE over prose because the runtime reader is a mid-tier model (aws/gpt-oss-120b). No val result yet (harness scores after stop) — cannot cite LEDGER rows.
- Verification approach that worked well: running each edited tool body against the live tau2 airline DB in the project venv on the EXACT failing-trace args, then re-running on a passing task's args to prove the guard is a no-op there. This is the cheapest way to satisfy the REAL+SAFE+VERIFIED bar without a full eval.
- Plateau/stall signal: n/a (first iteration).
- What to try next iteration:
  - Read this candidate's RESULT first. The riskiest bet is the no-write stall being fixable by prose — the tools skill explicitly says `narrated_without_action` resists prompt reminders. If cluster 1 tasks (8/12/17/19/40) don't move, switch that lever to a composite atomic-write tool (confirm+execute as one call) rather than adding more prompt text.
  - Keep candidates structurally distinct: if enriched returns + payment auto-fill are accepted, do NOT re-propose them; build the next candidate on a different cluster (task 22 route-matching resolver, or the cabin/cancel decision) with a narrowly-scoped guard.
  - Meta: verifying via direct tool-body execution against the DB is high-signal and cheap — keep doing it every iteration before shipping.

## Iteration cand_0002
- Strategy tried: broad multi-cluster candidate — 3 real CODE edits (new `list_reservations` loop tool, `cancel_reservation` flown guard, `update_reservation_passengers` dob auto-fill) + 5 tightly-scoped additive policy rules, covering all 6 failing clusters instead of just the top one. Verified every code edit by executing the tool body on the exact failing-trace args against the live DB, then a no-op check on gold/passing args — this direct-execution loop is fast and gives a real SAFE signal without a full eval.
- Parallelism paid off: 4 read-only diagnostic subagents (one per task-group) ran concurrently and produced argument-level root causes + a blast-radius recon of the passing tasks (11/25), which let me confirm the untouched write tools keep their exact output. Recommend keeping this fan-out pattern.
- Key realization: the biggest always-failing cluster (17/22) is not a rule violation the agent skips — it's a genuine capability/knowledge gap (no route-search; defaults to first reservation). A loop tool that surfaces routes in city terms lets the weak reader reason "to Chicago = ORD" instead of me hard-coding a fragile metro-area map.
- What to try next iteration: read this RESULT. If 17/22 still fail, escalate to a deterministic `find_reservation(user_id, origin/destination)` with a metro-area alias map. Do NOT re-add execute-on-yes prose (cand_0001 already has it; the ###STOP### cases look like a simulator artifact, not a fixable behavior).

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

## Iteration cand_0003 (LAST of run)
- Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: AMPLIFY-not-redesign. cand_0002 was rejected at Δ+0.083 with broke={—}; the framework verdict was explicit — "the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign; keep the edits." So I kept every cand_0002 edit and strengthened only the two with the weakest reasoning burden on the mid-tier runtime: (1) list_reservations→deterministic find_reservation with a metro-area map, (2) flown-only cancel guard→full 4-condition eligibility gate. RESULT pending (run may end here).
- Plateau/stall signal + lever switched to: the stall was NOT damage (nothing broke across cand_0001→0002) — it was effect SIZE below the significance bar. Correct meta-move: concentrate the effect on the clusters with a clean DETERMINISTIC fix (route resolution, cancel eligibility) instead of adding more thin, reason-dependent prose across all 6 clusters. Diagnosis: spreading edits thin dilutes per-task delta; a rejected-on-significance candidate wants depth on few tasks, not breadth.
- Highest-signal process lesson of the run: for a weak runtime reader (aws/gpt-oss-120b), DECIDE in code (find_reservation returns the answer) rather than surfacing structured data for it to reason over (list_reservations). The same edit-space intent can pass or fail purely on how much reasoning it offloads.
- What to try next run (if any): (1) if find_reservation still under-moves, fold resolution INTO the write tools so a wrong reservation_id is impossible to pass. (2) Ask the framework for MORE TRIALS in one eval on a known-good-but-rejected candidate before redesigning — cand_0002 may have been a true improvement lost to noise. (3) The ###STOP### no-write cases are a simulator artifact (no post-confirmation turn) — stop spending edits on them; see FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md.
- Verification loop (direct tool-body execution against the live DB, fire-case + no-op case) remained the single highest-value practice every iteration — cheap, high-signal, caught the earlier datetime-parse over-refusal bug before it shipped.
